chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us (Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on his authority), saying: Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, and I asked him about the Imamate, regarding whom it is obligatory, and what is the sign of the one to whom the Imamate is due?

He said: Indeed, the proof thereof, and the argument over the believers, and the one in charge of the affairs of the Muslims, and the speaker of the Quran, and the knower of the decrees, is the brother of God's Prophet, His Caliph over His nation, His testamentary executor over them, and His guardian who is to him in the same position as Aaron was to Moses,
Obedience to him is obligatory by the word of God, the Exalted: 'O you who believe! Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and those charged with authority among you.'

Described by His word: 'Only is your guardian Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe, those who establish prayer and give alms-tax while they bow down.' He is the one invited to by guardianship, the one whose Imamate was established on the day of Ghadir Khum by the word of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) from God, the Exalted: 'Am I not more entitled to you than your own selves?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then whoever I am his master, Ali is his master. O God, befriend whoever befriends him, and be enemy to whoever opposes him, and support whoever supports him, and abandon whoever abandons him, and help whoever helps him. Ali ibn Abi Talib is the Commander of the Faithful and the Imam of the Pious, and the Leader of the Fair-foreheaded, and the best of the Trustees, and the best of all creation after the Messenger.'

And after him, his son al-Hasan ibn Ali, then al-Husayn, the grandsons of God's Messenger and the sons of the best of all women. Then Ali ibn al-Husayn, then Muhammad ibn Ali, then Ja'far ibn Muhammad, then Musa ibn Ja'far, then Ali ibn Musa, then Muhammad ibn Ali, then Ali ibn Muhammad, then al-Hasan ibn Ali. Then Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, peace be upon them, up to our day. This is one after another, and they are the Progeny of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), known by the Testament and the Imamate. The Earth is never devoid of a Proof from among them in every era and time, and in every moment and occasion. They are the Firm Handhold, the Leaders of Guidance, and the Proof over the people of the world until God inherits the Earth and whoever is on it.

And whoever opposes them is deviant and misleading, abandoning the truth and guidance. They are the interpreters of the Quran and the speakers for the Messenger. Whoever dies not knowing them dies a death of Ignorance. Their religion is piety, chastity, honesty, righteousness, and striving. And fulfilling the trust to the righteous and the wicked. And long prostration. And standing in prayer at night. And avoiding the forbidden things. And waiting for the Relief with patience. And good companionship. And good neighborliness.
Then Tamim ibn Buhlool said: Abu Mu'awiah narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), regarding the Imamate, a similar narration, exactly the same.

key_terms.غَدِيرُ خَمٍّ: Ghadir Khum (the event where the Prophet appointed Ali)
key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: Death of Ignorance (pre-Islamic state of disbelief)

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Imams and what are the signs of the Imamate according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes the Imamate as a divine institution rooted in the event of Ghadir Khumm, where the Prophet explicitly designated Ali ibn Abi Talib as his successor. It enumerates the twelve Imams in unbroken succession, emphasizing their role as the 'Hujjah' (proof) of God on earth and the infallible interpreters of the Quran, thereby linking the concept of Wilayah directly to the verse of Wilayah (5:55) and the verse of Obedience (4:59).
